arxiv-2108-01257.title: A note on Haag duality
arxiv-2108-01257.creator: Alan Garbarz, Gabriel Palau
arxiv-2108-01257.description: Abstract Haag duality is a remarkable property in QFT stating that the commutant of the algebra of observables localized in some region of spacetime is exactly the algebra associated to the causally disconnected region. It is a strong condition on the local structure and has direct consequences on entanglement measures.

arxiv-2204-03357.title: Parameter-Efficient Abstractive Question Answering over Tables or Text
arxiv-2204-03357.creator: Vaishali Pal, Evangelos Kanoulas, Maarten de Rijke
arxiv-2204-03357.description: Abstract A long-term ambition of information seeking QA ( QA ) systems is to reason over multi-modal contexts and generate natural answers to user queries. Today, memory intensive pre-trained language models are adapted to downstream tasks such as QA by fine-tuning the model on QA data in a specific modality like unstructured text or structured tables.

arxiv-2312-02246.description: Abstract Inverse problems aim to determine parameters from observations, a crucial task in engineering and science. arxiv-2404-19297.title: Channel Performance Metrics and Evaluation for XR Head-Mounted Displays with mmWave Arrays
arxiv-2404-19297.creator: Alexander Marinšek, Xuesong Cai, Lieven De Strycker, Fredrik Tufvesson, Liesbet Van der Perre
arxiv-2404-19297.description: Abstract Millimeter-wave (mmWave) technology holds the potential to revolutionize head-mounted displays (HMDs) by enabling high-speed wireless communication with nearby processing nodes, where complex video rendering can take place. However, the sparse angular profile of mmWave channels, coupled with the narrow field of view (FoV) of patch-antenna arrays and frequent HMD rotation, can lead to poor performance.

Our results demonstrate robust Pareto efficiency compared to prior methods, translating to a 1.

arxiv-2503-08183.title: Physics-based AI methodology for Material Parameter Extraction from Optical Data
arxiv-2503-08183.creator: M. Koumans and J.L.M. van Mechelen
arxiv-2503-08183.description: Abstract We report on a novel methodology for extracting material parameters from spectroscopic optical data using a physics-based neural network. The proposed model integrates classical optimization frameworks with a multi-scale object detection framework, specifically exploring the effect of incorporating physics into the neural network. We validate and analyze its performance on simulated transmission spectra at terahertz and infrared frequencies.

arxiv-2509-02594.title: OpenAI’s HealthBench in Action: Evaluating an LLM-Based Medical Assistant on Realistic Clinical Queries
arxiv-2509-02594.creator: Sandhanakrishnan Ravichandran, Shivesh Kumar, Rogério Corga Da Silva, Miguel Romano, Reinhard Berkels, Michiel van der Heijden, Olivier Fail, Valentine Emmanuel Gnanapragasam
arxiv-2509-02594.description: Abstract Evaluating large language models (LLMs) on their ability to generate high-quality, accurate, situationally aware answers to clinical questions requires going beyond conventional benchmarks to assess how these systems behave in complex, high-stake clincal scenarios. Traditional evaluations are often limited to multiple-choice questions that fail to capture essential competencies such as contextual reasoning, awareness and uncertainty handling etc.

arxiv-2601-17133.title: Learning to Collaborate: An Orchestrated-Decentralized Framework for Peer-to-Peer LLM Federation
arxiv-2601-17133.creator: Inderjeet Singh, Eleonore Vissol-Gaudin, Andikan Otung, Motoyoshi Sekiya
arxiv-2601-17133.description: Abstract Fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) for specialized domains is constrained by a fundamental challenge: the need for diverse, cross-organizational data conflicts with the principles of data privacy and sovereignty. While Federated Learning (FL) provides a framework for collaboration without raw data exchange, its classic centralized form introduces a single point of failure and remains vulnerable to model inversion attacks.
